thread:
Marco: fyi I hit a race in a deadline-transfer soak: gateway marked req as timed_out but edge still streamed ~800ms of tokens. reproducer below.

Sara: logs? hedging path? :thinking: 

Marco: logs (short):
```
gateway: deadline -> abort intent
gateway: request -> timed_out
edge: upstream kept sending chunks (~800ms)
edge: returned 499 to client
```

Lin: sounds like abort visibility is asymmetric. trailers are flaky; TCP buffering possible. Gateway finalizes billing/fallback before edge terminal event.

Kevin: recall contract allowed a short grace window for in-flight tokens. Maybe billing/obs doesn't honor it.

Sara: options: (1) gateway drains for 300-1000ms before finalizing; or (2) control-plane terminal event from edge (preferred).

Lin: propose control messages: gateway publishes `control.abort_intent` with trace_id+req_id; edge replies with `control.stream_term` when it hits terminal state (stream_end, error, client_close). Gateway waits up to config timeout (default 500ms) before finalizing. Observability should use edge terminal event when present.

Marco: hedging: edge must include per-upstream stream_id; report each stream_end. Gateway aggregates. Also avoid triggering stateful retries until stream_term or timeout.

Kevin: pubsub reordering concern: messages must be idempotent and include attempt counters. Add jitter to drain timers to avoid thundering herd.

Sara: rollout: opt-in flag on some ingress gateways, 2-week canary; add metric `post_abort_tokens_returned`.

Marco: sample control messages:
`{"type":"control.abort_intent","trace_id":"t-abc","req_id":"r-123","ts":"2026-03-21T18:16:17Z"}`
reply:
`{"type":"control.stream_term","trace_id":"t-abc","req_id":"r-123","stream_id":"s-1","final_status":"ok","ts":"2026-03-21T18:16:17.143Z"}`

Ops Bot: feature flag `edge-drain-window` scheduled in canary 2026-03-28. :white_check_mark:
